title: Runbook: Backfill & recompute Usage Insights aggregates (route/model dimensions)
author: Mei Lin
content:
## Overview
This runbook describes how to backfill new dimensions (notably `route` and `model`) into Usage Insights aggregates and safely recompute affected materializations.

Usage Insights is built from metering/telemetry events and aggregated into hourly and daily rollups used by the Console and the export/reporting APIs. When we introduce a new dimension, fix a normalization bug, or change a cost attribution algorithm, we may need to:
- Recompute aggregates for a bounded time window.
- Backfill only the affected partitions.
- Validate results against source-of-truth metering.
- Roll back quickly if cardinality, correctness, or query latency regress.

This runbook assumes the standard pipeline:
- Event ingestion: `metering-ingest` → `telemetry-events` (raw)
- Normalization: `usage-insights-normalizer`
- Aggregation: `usage-insights-aggregator` (hourly + daily)
- Serving: `insights-api` reads aggregated tables/materialized views

## When to use this runbook
Use this runbook when any of the following are true:
1) A new dimension is added (e.g., `route`, `model_variant`, `deployment_mode`).
2) Normalization rules change (e.g., route canonicalization v1 → v2).
3) Aggregation logic changes (e.g., cached token attribution fix).
4) Late-arriving metering events require recompute for a specific window.
5) A data incident requires correcting a known-bad partition.

Do NOT use this runbook for:
- Routine daily rollups (handled automatically by scheduled jobs).
- Long-range historical rebuilds beyond retention without explicit approval (see “Approvals & guardrails”).

## Approvals & guardrails
Backfills are high-risk due to cost, cardinality blow-ups, and customer-facing inconsistencies.

Required before executing in production:
- Approver: Eng lead for Telemetry/Analytics (Logan Wright) OR on-call incident commander during an active incident.
- Reviewer: SRE/Observability (Allison Grant) for any backfill > 7 days or any job expected to exceed 30 minutes.
- Security review is NOT required unless backfill changes export behavior or RBAC boundaries.

Hard guardrails:
- Max backfill window per run: 14 days (unless explicitly approved by Logan + SRE).
- Max concurrent partitions: 48 hourly partitions OR 14 daily partitions.
- Cancel criteria: any of the following triggers immediate pause/cancel:
  - Route cardinality alarm fires (see “Monitoring”).
  - `insights-api` p95 latency increases > 25% over baseline for 15 minutes.
  - ClickHouse insert latency > 60s sustained for 10 minutes.

## Preconditions / access
You need:
- Production read access to raw metering tables and write access to aggregate tables.
- Kubernetes access to the `analytics-prod` cluster.
- Ability to run `redwoodctl` (internal ops CLI) with role `analytics-operator`.

Set environment:
- Prod cluster: `analytics-prod`
- Namespace: `usage-insights`
- ClickHouse cluster: `ch-analytics-prod`

Helpful aliases:
- `export RW_ENV=prod`
- `export RW_CLUSTER=analytics-prod`

## Data model & tables (high-level)
Raw inputs:
- `telemetry_events.metering_events_v2` (append-only)

Aggregates (serving inputs):
- `usage_insights.route_model_hourly_v1`
- `usage_insights.route_model_daily_v1`

Serving views (stable API target; may point to different backing tables during migrations):
- `usage_insights.route_model_hourly`
- `usage_insights.route_model_daily`

Notes:
- Hourly rollups are used for recent ranges and sparklines; daily rollups are used for longer ranges.
- All aggregates are partitioned by `dt` (YYYY-MM-DD) and optionally `hr` (0–23).

## Monitoring to have open during execution
Open these before starting (dashboards are referenced in the backend health dashboards page):
- Pipeline lag: `usage-insights-normalizer` and `usage-insights-aggregator`
- ClickHouse health: merges, insert latency, replication queue
- `insights-api` p95 and error rate
- Cardinality alarms: distinct routes per org/project per day

Also tail job logs while running:
- `kubectl -n usage-insights logs -f deploy/usage-insights-aggregator`
- `kubectl -n usage-insights logs -f deploy/usage-insights-normalizer`

## Step 0 — Confirm the reason and choose the backfill strategy
Pick ONE of the following strategies:

A) Recompute aggregates from raw events (preferred)
- Use when normalization or attribution changed.
- Most correct; more expensive.

B) Backfill missing dimension values only
- Use when raw events already contain required info and only aggregates are missing columns.
- Typically only safe for additive columns (e.g., a derived boolean) and when aggregation keys do not change.

For `route`/`model` changes, use Strategy A unless explicitly approved otherwise.

## Step 1 — Define the target scope
Define:
- Time window: start/end date (and optionally hours)
- Tenancy: all orgs OR a limited set (recommended for first run)
- Deployment mode: hosted/dedicated/private if limiting is supported

Example scope definition (recommended first run):
- 1 day in prod, limited to 1–3 internal orgs
- Then expand to 3 days
- Then expand to full approved window

Record the scope in the change ticket / incident doc:
- Reason
- Start/end
- Expected partitions count
- Expected cost impact (rough)

## Step 2 — Put the system in a safe operational mode
1) Ensure the Console feature flag (route insights) is stable.
- If you are recomputing behind the same serving view, consider temporarily disabling customer exposure:
  - Toggle feature flag `console_usage_insights_route_cost_drivers` OFF for external orgs if recompute could cause inconsistent numbers.

2) Reduce aggregator concurrency (optional but recommended for > 3 days).
- Set `AGGREGATOR_MAX_PARTITIONS_IN_FLIGHT=2` (or lower) via deployment override.

3) Confirm there is no ongoing schema migration.
- Check that ClickHouse DDL migrations are green and no long-running ALTERs exist.

## Step 3 — Dry-run cardinality and estimated volume
Before writing anything, run estimation queries to avoid cardinality blow-ups.

Example (ClickHouse) — estimate distinct routes in scope:
- `SELECT dt, countDistinct(route) AS distinct_routes FROM telemetry_events.metering_events_v2 WHERE dt BETWEEN '2026-02-01' AND '2026-02-03' AND org_id IN ('org_123') GROUP BY dt ORDER BY dt;`

Example — top routes by count (spot dynamic IDs):
- `SELECT route, count() AS n FROM telemetry_events.metering_events_v2 WHERE dt='2026-02-02' AND org_id='org_123' GROUP BY route ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 50;`

If distinct routes exceeds the published budget (see cardinality standards), STOP and escalate to Thomas Baird.

## Step 4 — Execute the backfill (recommended path: workflow-driven)
We run recomputes via a workflow to ensure:
- Partition-by-partition progress tracking
- Rate limiting
- Automatic retry with jitter
- Safe cancellation

### 4.1 Create a backfill plan
Create a plan file locally for auditability:

Plan format (YAML stored in the change ticket attachment):
- name: ui-route-model-recompute-2026-02-21
- window_start: 2026-02-01T00:00:00Z
- window_end: 2026-02-04T00:00:00Z
- granularity: hourly
- org_allowlist: [org_123]
- write_mode: shadow
- route_normalization_version: v2
- max_partitions_in_flight: 2

Notes:
- `write_mode=shadow` writes to `*_v1_shadow` tables and does not affect serving until promoted.
- Use `write_mode=in_place` only for emergency fixes where shadowing is not available.

### 4.2 Start the workflow
Command:
- `redwoodctl usage-insights backfill start --plan ./ui-route-model-recompute-2026-02-21.yaml`

Check status:
- `redwoodctl usage-insights backfill status --name ui-route-model-recompute-2026-02-21`

Tail workflow logs:
- `redwoodctl usage-insights backfill logs --name ui-route-model-recompute-2026-02-21 --follow`

### 4.3 If you must run manually (last resort)
Only use this if workflows are down and an incident requires immediate correction.

1) Pause scheduled aggregation for the target partitions to avoid contention.
2) Run the partition job:
- `kubectl -n usage-insights create job --from=cronjob/usage-insights-aggregate-hourly usage-insights-aggregate-hourly-manual-20260202-13`
3) Set env overrides (example):
- `BACKFILL_DT=2026-02-02`
- `BACKFILL_HR=13`
- `ROUTE_NORMALIZATION_VERSION=v2`
- `WRITE_TARGET=route_model_hourly_v1_shadow`

Escalate to SRE if you need to do this for more than 2 partitions.

## Step 5 — Promote shadow tables to serving (cutover)
Do not cut over until validations pass.

Promotion procedure:
1) Confirm shadow completeness for the window:
- `SELECT count() FROM usage_insights.route_model_hourly_v1_shadow WHERE dt BETWEEN '2026-02-01' AND '2026-02-03';`

2) Atomically swap serving view to point to shadow (implementation varies; standard is view swap):
- `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW usage_insights.route_model_hourly AS SELECT * FROM usage_insights.route_model_hourly_v1_shadow;`
- `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW usage_insights.route_model_daily AS SELECT * FROM usage_insights.route_model_daily_v1_shadow;`

3) Purge/refresh API caches if applicable:
- `redwoodctl insights-api cache purge --scope usage-insights --window 2026-02-01..2026-02-03`

4) Re-enable any feature flags if you disabled them.

## Step 6 — Validation checklist (must-pass)
Validation must be performed for:
- At least 2 internal orgs (or the org(s) in scope)
- At least 2 different routes
- At least 2 different models (including a fallback path if possible)

### 6.1 Row-level sanity checks
- No negative token counts
- No negative cost values
- Latency fields in expected ranges (p50 <= p95, non-null if requests exist)

Example:
- `SELECT count() FROM usage_insights.route_model_hourly WHERE (input_tokens < 0 OR output_tokens < 0 OR total_cost_usd < 0) AND dt BETWEEN '2026-02-01' AND '2026-02-03';`
Expected: 0

### 6.2 Completeness vs raw metering totals (tolerance-based)
Compare total cost and tokens aggregated vs raw metering within tolerance.

Recommended tolerances (due to late events and rounding):
- Cost: within 0.5% for completed windows older than 24h
- Tokens: within 0.5%

Example (per org per day):
- Raw:
  - `SELECT dt, org_id, sum(total_cost_usd) AS raw_cost FROM telemetry_events.metering_events_v2 WHERE dt BETWEEN '2026-02-01' AND '2026-02-03' AND org_id='org_123' GROUP BY dt, org_id;`
- Agg:
  - `SELECT dt, org_id, sum(total_cost_usd) AS agg_cost FROM usage_insights.route_model_daily WHERE dt BETWEEN '2026-02-01' AND '2026-02-03' AND org_id='org_123' GROUP BY dt, org_id;`

If outside tolerance:
- Check pipeline lag and late-arriving events.
- Confirm the same filtering rules are applied (e.g., excluding internal test traffic).
- Confirm route normalization version.
- If still off, STOP and escalate to Nadia Rahman.

### 6.3 Cardinality checks post-recompute
Verify route cardinality is within budget.

Example:
- `SELECT dt, org_id, countDistinct(route) AS distinct_routes FROM usage_insights.route_model_daily WHERE dt BETWEEN '2026-02-01' AND '2026-02-03' GROUP BY dt, org_id ORDER BY distinct_routes DESC LIMIT 20;`

If you see spikes:
- Identify offending routes (often unbounded values like user IDs).
- Confirm normalizer hashing/rollup behavior is active.
- Consider backfilling again after applying stricter normalization.

### 6.4 Serving/API verification
Use the API to validate the console view:
- Top routes endpoint returns data for the backfilled window.
- Route detail shows model breakdown.
- Pagination and sorting behave as expected.

Smoke test (internal):
- `redwoodctl insights-api smoke-test --org org_123 --window 2026-02-01..2026-02-03 --checks top-routes,route-detail,export-dry-run`

## Step 7 — Post-backfill cleanup
After successful promotion:
- Keep shadow tables for 7 days (default) for rollback safety.
- Annotate dashboard with a change marker (include backfill name + window).
- Update the support/CS known-issues page if numbers changed materially (e.g., route attribution correction).

## Rollback plan
Rollback is required if:
- API p95 latency regression persists beyond 30 minutes after cutover.
- Cardinality alarms fire and cannot be mitigated quickly.
- Validation reveals material correctness issues.

Rollback steps (serving cutover rollback):
1) Disable customer exposure (if applicable):
- Feature flag `console_usage_insights_route_cost_drivers` OFF for external orgs.

2) Swap views back to previous stable backing tables:
- `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW usage_insights.route_model_hourly AS SELECT * FROM usage_insights.route_model_hourly_v1;`
- `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW usage_insights.route_model_daily AS SELECT * FROM usage_insights.route_model_daily_v1;`

3) Purge API caches:
- `redwoodctl insights-api cache purge --scope usage-insights --window 2026-02-01..2026-02-03`

4) Cancel running workflows/jobs:
- `redwoodctl usage-insights backfill cancel --name ui-route-model-recompute-2026-02-21`

5) Preserve evidence:
- Save logs and the plan file in the incident/change ticket.
- Capture “before/after” metrics screenshots for SRE.

Do NOT immediately drop shadow partitions; keep them for investigation unless storage is under pressure.

## Common failure modes & mitigations
1) Export job timeouts during recompute
- Symptom: exports fail while ClickHouse is busy merging.
- Mitigation: throttle backfill concurrency, temporarily reduce export max rows/time range, or pause exports via feature flag.

2) “Unknown route” dominates
- Symptom: route tagging missing, gateway derivation not enabled, or normalization collapsing to unknown.
- Mitigation: validate SDK header adoption, check gateway config, ensure route derivation middleware is enabled.

3) Costs don’t match invoice totals
- Symptom: customers compare console insights to billing exports.
- Mitigation: confirm time window alignment, late-arriving events cutoff, and retention behavior; reference the support known-issues doc.

4) Cardinality explosion
- Symptom: distinct routes spike, query latency increases.
- Mitigation: enable/verify normalization rollups, enforce length limits, hash unknown patterns, and consider dropping offending partitions and re-running.

## Operational notes
- Always backfill from oldest → newest partitions to minimize mismatch with late events.
- Avoid running large recomputes during peak traffic hours (typically 16:00–23:00 UTC).
- Prefer shadow + promote over in-place recompute to minimize customer-visible inconsistency.

## Appendix: quick command reference
Kubernetes:
- `kubectl config use-context analytics-prod`
- `kubectl -n usage-insights get pods`
- `kubectl -n usage-insights logs -f deploy/usage-insights-aggregator`

redwoodctl:
- `redwoodctl usage-insights backfill start --plan <file>`
- `redwoodctl usage-insights backfill status --name <name>`
- `redwoodctl usage-insights backfill cancel --name <name>`
- `redwoodctl insights-api cache purge --scope usage-insights --window <start>..<end>`

ClickHouse sanity:
- `SELECT max(updated_at) FROM usage_insights.route_model_hourly;`
- `SELECT dt, sum(total_cost_usd) FROM usage_insights.route_model_daily GROUP BY dt ORDER BY dt DESC LIMIT 14;`
